literal: Even if a fault as small as a millet seed comes, those who fear disgrace will consider it as large as a palmyra palm.
translation: Those who shrink from disgrace will regard a fault as huge as a palmyra palm, even if it is as tiny as a millet seed.
modern: பழிக்கு அஞ்சுகின்றவர்கள், தினை அளவு சிறிய குற்றம் தமக்கு நேர்ந்தாலும், அதனைப் பனை மர அளவு பெரியதாகக் கருதி எச்சரிக்கையோடு இருப்பார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the extreme vigilance of noble people who dread disgrace. The poet contrasts two well-known objects of vastly different sizes: the tiny millet seed ('தினை') and the massive palmyra palm ('பனை'). Those who fear blame ('பழிநாணுவார்') do not ignore even the smallest slip-up; instead, they treat a minuscule error as a monumental disaster. By magnifying their own minor faults, they actively correct themselves and preserve their flawless character.
